Craig’s actual-infinite-to-finite-past inference and its concrete and methodological support are directly represented.
Hilbert’s Hotel, the defense of finitism as the triad’s resolution, and the checkout cases jointly represent Craig’s concrete-impossibility case.
The successive-addition inference, countdown objection, restricted explanatory demand, and Grim Reaper paradox cover Craig’s stated support for this route.
Craig’s eternal-or-never objection to an impersonal mechanism and his defense of coherent timeless personhood represent the personal-cause inference.
Malpass’s challenges to the causal premise, finite-past arguments, and personal-cause analysis collectively express why he regards the Kalam’s complete conclusion as unestablished.
Selected con-side moves preserve beginningless material and non-metric alternatives while also preserving an impersonal-origin alternative.
Malpass’s qualified concession, infinite-set analysis, linguistic resolution, and relative-complement reply distinguish strangeness from impossibility.
The endpoint asymmetry, necessary-versus-sufficient diagnosis, and partial-explanation answer directly represent Malpass’s response to the countdown argument.
Malpass supplies both an impersonal indeterministic origin model and a separate coherence objection to the changeless personal alternative.
